data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's central mechanism attributes the reliability gain to 'cognitive friction' that forces serial verification and eliminates expert blind spots. But the problem specifically demands that the argument identify what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. SRC_001's mechanism gives no diagnostic criterion: any observed correctness of the panel is equally consistent with (a) genuine friction-driven error correction and (b) rote checklist adherence that coincidentally matches the verifiable outcome. The counterconditions (vague checklist causing semantic drift; holistic-synthesis tasks) describe failure modes, not the discriminating evidence the problem asks for. A single evaluation showing the panel outperforming the expert could not, per SRC_001's own mechanism, separate whether the gain came from friction-recovered visibility versus the checklist simply encoding the answer path—which is precisely the confound the problem requires the argument to address.
